scope: Additional safe classroom experiment concepts only.

experiments.title: Temperature and flow observation
experiments.focus: Show that water can behave differently when it is warmer or cooler.
student_observations: Liquid behavior can change with temperature.
Warm liquids may appear to move differently from cool ones.
Temperature is a useful physical property.
experiments.teacher_note: Keep the example conceptual and simple.

experiments.title: Melting and reforming review
experiments.focus: Review that a material can melt and then form the solid again when conditions change.
student_observations: Ice becomes liquid water.
Cooling can reverse the change in the model.
The substance stays the same while the state changes.
experiments.teacher_note: Useful as a simple recap of phase change.

experiments.title: Water drop and surface review
experiments.focus: Show that a tiny amount of soap can change how water behaves at the surface.
student_observations: Small additions can change the surface behavior.
Bubbles may form more easily.
Everyday materials can affect physical properties.
experiments.teacher_note: A quick demo for physical properties.

experiments.title: Fine vs coarse particle mixture
experiments.focus: Compare how small and large particles behave in water.
student_observations: Different particles can make the mixture look different.
Some mixtures stay cloudy longer.
Particle size matters in mixtures.

experiments.title: Filtering concept review
experiments.focus: Introduce the idea that some mixtures can be separated by filtration.
student_observations: Solid particles can be held back by a filter.
The liquid can pass through.
Filtration is a useful separation method.
experiments.teacher_note: Keep it as a concept demo in the virtual model.

experiments.title: Dilution with water
experiments.focus: Show that adding more water can make a solution less concentrated.
student_observations: The same substance can be spread through more water.
Color or taste is not needed to discuss concentration.
Dilution changes concentration, not the identity of the substance.
experiments.teacher_note: Useful for introducing concentration in simple words.

experiments.title: Mixture separation by settling
experiments.focus: Show that heavier particles can settle to the bottom over time.
student_observations: Particles may move downward over time.
The top liquid can become clearer.
Settling is another separation idea.
experiments.teacher_note: Pairs well with filtration and suspension review.

experiments.title: Diffusion in water concept
experiments.focus: Show how a colored substance can spread through water on its own.
student_observations: The color spreads without stirring in the model.
Particles move from one area to another.
Diffusion happens in many everyday situations.

experiments.title: Syrup viscosity concept
experiments.focus: Compare how thick liquids flow more slowly than thin liquids.
student_observations: Some liquids flow more slowly.
Thickness is a physical property.
Viscosity can be compared in a model.
experiments.teacher_note: A good bridge to the idea of viscosity.

experiments.title: Mix and separate review
experiments.focus: Review several mixture types in one classroom activity.
student_observations: Some mixtures form layers.
Some mixtures look cloudy.
Some materials dissolve to make clear solutions.
experiments.teacher_note: Useful as a recap before senior-level concepts.

experiments.title: Evaporation speed comparison
experiments.focus: Show that warmer conditions can make evaporation happen faster in the model.
student_observations: Water can leave the container at different speeds.
Temperature can affect the rate.
Evaporation is a physical process.
experiments.teacher_note: Keep the explanation simple and visual.

experiments.title: Chromatography concept review
experiments.focus: Introduce the idea that mixed colors can separate because different parts move differently.
student_observations: A mixed color can separate into parts.
Different components can move at different speeds.
Chromatography is a separation idea.
experiments.teacher_note: Use as a conceptual example only.

experiments.title: Concentration comparison review
experiments.focus: Compare a weak and a strong solution in the classroom model.
student_observations: The same solute can be spread in different amounts of water.
Concentration changes the appearance of a solution in the model.
The amount of solute matters.
experiments.teacher_note: Useful for a first-pass concentration lesson.

experiments.title: Temperature and solubility review
experiments.focus: Discuss how temperature can be linked to solubility ideas in the classroom model.
student_observations: Temperature can matter in dissolution models.
Different substances can behave differently.
Solubility is a property worth comparing.

experiments.title: Particle size and dissolving review
experiments.focus: Compare how particle size can affect the way substances behave in water.
student_observations: Some solids dissolve, some stay visible.
Particle size can affect the appearance of the mixture.
Not all powders behave the same way.
experiments.teacher_note: Great for revision and sorting activities.

experiments.title: Density layer review
experiments.focus: Show that liquids can layer depending on density and miscibility.
student_observations: Liquids may separate into layers.
Density helps explain the order of layers.
Not all liquids mix evenly.

experiments.title: Precipitation and solution review
experiments.focus: Review that some mixtures can turn cloudy because a new solid forms.
student_observations: A clear mixture can become cloudy.
A solid product can appear in the model.
Not every reaction stays invisible.
experiments.teacher_note: Tie this directly to the validated reaction registry.

experiments.title: Separation methods overview
experiments.focus: Compare filtration, settling, evaporation and layer separation as classroom methods.
student_observations: Different mixtures need different separation ideas.
Some methods work on solids in liquids.
Some methods work on liquids that do not mix.

experiments.title: Reversible vs irreversible review
experiments.focus: Classify a few classroom changes by whether they can be undone in the model.
student_observations: Some changes can be reversed.
Some changes are just state changes.
Some changes are better described as mixture changes.
